# nobias-fht/denoisesegment [![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open_In_GitHub_Codespaces-black?labelColor=grey&logo=github)](https://github.com/codespaces/new/nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo) [![GitHub Actions CI Status](https://github.com/nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo/actions/workflows/nf-test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo/actions/workflows/nf-test.yml) [![GitHub Actions Linting Status](https://github.com/nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo/actions/workflows/linting.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo/actions/workflows/linting.yml) [![nf-test](https://img.shields.io/badge/unit_tests-nf--test-337ab7.svg)](https://www.nf-test.com) [![Nextflow](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-%E2%89%A525.10.4-green?style=flat&logo=nextflow&logoColor=white&color=%230DC09D&link=https%3A%2F%2Fnextflow.io)](https://www.nextflow.io/) [![nf-core template version](https://img.shields.io/badge/nf--core_template-4.2.1-green?style=flat&logo=nfcore&logoColor=white&color=%2324B064&link=https%3A%2F%2Fnf-co.re)](https://github.com/nf-core/tools/releases/tag/4.2.1) [![run with conda](http://img.shields.io/badge/run%20with-conda-3EB049?labelColor=000000&logo=anaconda)](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/) [![run with docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/run%20with-docker-0db7ed?labelColor=000000&logo=docker)](https://www.docker.com/) [![run with singularity](https://img.shields.io/badge/run%20with-singularity-1d355c.svg?labelColor=000000)](https://sylabs.io/docs/) [![Launch on Seqera Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Launch%20%F0%9F%9A%80-Seqera%20Platform-%234256e7)](https://cloud.seqera.io/launch?pipeline=https://github.com/nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo) ## Introduction **nobias-fht/denoisesegment** is an image-analysis pipeline that denoises TIFF microscopy images and then produces instance segmentations of cells. It trains a self-supervised [Noise2Void (N2V)](https://careamics.github.io/) model with CAREamics on the supplied images, applies the trained model to those images, and passes each denoised TIFF to [Cellpose](https://www.cellpose.org/) to generate labelled segmentation masks. ```mermaid flowchart LR images[/TIFF image or directory/]:::input val[/Optional validation image or directory/]:::input config_params[/Axes, patch size, batch size
and optional N2V settings/]:::input cellpose_params[/Optional Cellpose settings/]:::input subgraph n2v[IMAGE_TRAIN_PREDICT_N2V_CAREAMICS subworkflow] config[CAREAMICS_CONFIGN2V] subgraph train_predict[IMAGE_TRAIN_PREDICT_CAREAMICS subworkflow] train[CAREAMICS_TRAIN] predict[CAREAMICS_PREDICT] end config -->|careamics.yaml| train train -->|selected checkpoint| predict end config_params --> config images -->|training data| train val -.->|validation data| train images -->|prediction data| predict train --> checkpoints[(Model checkpoints)]:::output train --> metrics[(Training metrics)]:::output predict --> denoised[(Denoised TIFF images)]:::output denoised --> cellpose[CELLPOSE] cellpose_params --> cellpose cellpose --> masks[(Labelled mask TIFFs)]:::output classDef input fill:#fff4dd,stroke:#d89b29,color:#111; classDef output fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#43a047,color:#111; ``` The default analysis steps are: 1. Create an N2V configuration from the required CAREamics parameters. 2. Train CAREamics on the input TIFF data, optionally using separate validation data. 3. Select the checkpoint recorded by CAREamics and use it to denoise the input data. 4. Run Cellpose independently on each denoised image and publish the labelled masks. The main inputs and outputs are described in more detail in the [usage](docs/usage.md) and [output](docs/output.md) documentation. ## Usage > [!NOTE] > If you are new to Nextflow and nf-core, please refer to the [nf-core environment setup documentation](https://nf-co.re/docs/get_started/environment_setup/overview) before running the workflow. Provide `--input` as either one TIFF file or a directory containing TIFF images. You must also describe the image axes and choose the spatial patch size and batch size used by CAREamics. For example: ```bash nextflow run nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo \ -profile \ --input path/to/images \ --outdir \ --careamics_axes CYX \ --careamics_patch_size "64 64" \ --careamics_batch_size 64 \ --careamics_n_channels 2 ``` You can also use the nf-core launcher to more easily select parameters with: ```bash nf-core pipelines launch nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo ``` > [!WARNING] > Please provide pipeline parameters via the CLI or Nextflow `-params-file` option. Custom config files including those provided by the `-c` Nextflow option can be used to provide any configuration _**except for parameters**_; see [docs](https://nf-co.re/docs/running/run-pipelines#using-parameter-files). ## Example data Example data is available using the download script in [this GitHub gist](https://gist.github.com/melisande-c/bc2d3abe95eb8e66725e03e22e31eec0). Using `uv`, this can be run directly from GitHub with: ```bash uv run https://gist.githubusercontent.com/melisande-c/bc2d3abe95eb8e66725e03e22e31eec0/raw/919580897df22b44da6663173dca15ab55b979a8/download_example_jump.py ``` This downloads 10 two-channel images to `./data/example-jump` in the directory from which the script is run. The images have `CYX` axes, so `--careamics_n_channels 2` is required. A patch size of `64 64`, a batch size of `64`, and 20 training epochs are suggested for this small demonstration dataset: ```bash nextflow run nobias-fht/denoisesegment-nf-demo \ -profile docker \ --input ./data/example-jump \ --outdir ./results \ --careamics_axes CYX \ --careamics_n_channels 2 \ --careamics_patch_size "64 64" \ --careamics_batch_size 64 \ --careamics_num_epochs 20 ``` See the [usage documentation](docs/usage.md) for parameter-file and GPU-profile examples. ## Credits nobias-fht/denoisesegment was originally written by Melisande Croft. ## Contributions and Support If you would like to contribute to this pipeline, please see the [contributing guidelines](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Citations To cite this pipeline, use the metadata in [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff). Please also cite the software used in your analysis. An extensive list of references for the tools used by the pipeline can be found in the [`CITATIONS.md`](CITATIONS.md) file.
